first.text: You pull up a seat at the table. The Half-Orc opposite picks his teeth with a dagger.
'Ready?' he grumbles. He tosses you a stack of dice.
'What's the game?' you ask.
'Swindlestones,' the Half-Orc replies. 'A game of luck and brains.' He chuckles. 'And looks.'
'Tell me the rules.'

'You roll behind your hand. I roll behind mine. You say, "There are 2 ones on the table," or something like that. I call to say, no, I do not believe it - or I say something higher. Higher number, or more dice. When called, we see who is right. Loser loses dice. No dice, loser is loser.'
'I understand.'
'Is simple. Now, play.'
You gather up your five dice and throw them behind your palm, getting one 1, three 2s and one 4.
The Half-Orc rolls his five dice and snorts.
'Your bet first,' the Half-Orc grumbles.
'I bet one 1,' you declare.
'Let's see now,' the Half-Orc murmurs, scratching his chin with a hooked nail. 'I bet two 4s. Next, you.'
[ You have one 1, three 2s and one 4 ]
'I call,' you declare.
The dice are revealed. Alongside my one 1, three 2s and one 4, he has one 1, one 2 and three 4s. That puts four 4s on the table.
The Half-Orc nods in deep satisfaction, as you push one of your dice away.
You gather up your four dice and throw them behind your palm, getting two 1s, one 2 and one 4.
The Half-Orc rolls his five dice and chuckles.
'Let's see now,' the Half-Orc murmurs, scratching his chin with a hooked nail. 'I bet one 2. What say you?'
'I call,' you declare.
The dice are revealed. Alongside my two 1s, one 2 and one 4, he has one 2, two 3s and two 4s. That puts two 2s on the table.
The Half-Orc nods in deep satisfaction, as you push one of your dice away.
You gather up your three dice and throw them behind your palm, getting one 1 and two 3s.
The Half-Orc rolls his five dice and chuckles.
'Let's see now,' the Half-Orc murmurs, scratching his chin with a hooked nail. 'I bet three 4s. Now - you.'
'I call,' you declare.
The dice are revealed. Alongside my one 1 and two 3s, he has one 2, one 3 and three 4s. That puts three 4s on the table.
The Half-Orc nods in deep satisfaction, as you push one of your dice away.
You gather up your two dice and throw them behind your palm, getting one 1 and one 4.
The Half-Orc rolls his five dice and snorts.
'Let's see now,' the Half-Orc murmurs, scratching his chin with a hooked nail. 'I bet three 3s. Too big for you, I think.'
'I call,' you declare.
The dice are revealed. Alongside my one 1 and one 4, he has two 2s and three 3s. That puts three 3s on the table.
The Half-Orc nods in deep satisfaction, as you push one of your dice away.
You roll the remaining dice behind your palm, getting one 1.
The Half-Orc rolls his five dice and chuckles.
'Let's see now,' the Half-Orc murmurs, scratching his chin with a hooked nail. 'I bet one 1. You, now.'
'I call,' you declare.
The dice are revealed. Alongside my one 1, he has one 1, one 2, two 3s and one 4. That puts two 1s on the table.
You toss your last dice, and the creature reaches across the table to scoop the pile of gold into his lap.
'I say you loser from moment you sit on chair,' he grumbles with delight. 'Loser face.'
